_comment: Layered-architecture discipline over the LIVE manifest corpus (ADR-0148 Cilium L3/L4 + Istio Ambient L7, ADR-0182 gateway vs mesh, ADR-0183 Cedar vs Kyverno, ADR-0184 Valkey vs Memcached). Until governance/check/layered-architecture-discipline/tests/layered_architecture_discipline_live.rs landed, this doctrine had never produced a verdict about this codebase: the kernel's only Cargo consumer is marketplace/facade/dev-cli, which no workflow invokes, and that runner enumerates cloud/*/, oya/*/ and microservices/*/ only — three roots the ADR-0562 capability reorg moved the manifests out from under, so it would have audited almost nothing even if something had called it. The fixture suite in src/lib.rs is untouched; the live target was ADDED beside it. Both frozen maps are keyed `<declared microservice>::<ViolationKind>` and pinned by EQUALITY over the UNION of the frozen and observed key sets, and are therefore TWO-SIDED: a new violation blocks, and a repaired one ALSO blocks until its pin is lowered in the same change. The min_* floors count SUBJECT MATERIAL (tracked paths, manifest documents, audited identities), never findings, so none of them can red on honest progress; there is deliberately NO floor on any violation count and none on the deferral-ledger row count, because all of them have zero as their intended destination and a floor on a zero-target term reds exactly when the work succeeds.
subject: every tracked file whose BASENAME is manifest.json and which declares a `"microservice"` identity, grouped into one audited document per declared identity
_measured_2026_08_19: Measured on dev @ 889027711, the commit that deleted 51 unreferenced product crates and moved every corpus in this repository: 89 tracked manifest.json over 13746 tracked paths; 78 declare a `microservice` identity and group into 67 audited µservices; 11 declare none and are excluded. 9 violations — 2 active, 7 covered by the Wave-3-I deferral ledger. Small enough that a reviewer can open every subject file by hand, which is the point: this is a finding set that can be checked rather than trusted.
_identity_is_declared_not_inferred: 30 of the 89 manifests declare a `"microservice"` that differs from their directory leaf. gateway/manifest.json declares "api-gateway" — exactly the name ViolationKind::NorthSouthOnlyMisplaced exempts, and exactly the name the deferral ledger's `api-gateway GatewayAndMeshConflict` row is keyed on. Keying on the leaf would manufacture a violation against the one service the rule excuses AND un-suppress ledger rows keyed on declared names (`api-gateway GatewayAndMeshConflict`, `feature-flags MeshTierUnderclaimed`). Found the hard way in PR #2156; the walk reads the JSON key and never looks at the directory name.
_why_one_document_per_identity: ManifestDocument's own doc comment defines the calling convention as "the concatenated text plus the µservice name" — a µservice is described by several files. Two identities are spread over more than one manifest today: `developer-sdk` and `plugin-app-store` (a base manifest plus five regulatory pack overlays each). Auditing per FILE instead reports ten extra MeshTierUnderclaimed violations against pack overlays that carry no `mesh_layering` block because their base manifest already declares `cilium_l4: true` and `ambient_ztunnel: true` — ten findings whose only honest repair is "audit the µservice, not the fragment". What grouping costs, stated rather than papered over: concatenation can mask an under-claim (one fragment declares the tier for all of them) and can manufacture a conflict (two fragments each individually consistent, contradicting once merged). Both are properties of treating a µservice as the unit, which is what the doctrine is about. The census printed on every run lists every contributing path, so which files were merged is never a guess.
_the_two_active_findings_and_their_repai: cloud-os (os/manifest.json) declares `mesh_layering.cilium_l4: false` and `ambient_ztunnel: false` with `north_south_only` absent, alongside the non-claim "No pod, host, CNI, service mesh, or network policy runtime is deployed" — an honest scaffold declaration that the ADR-0148 rule has no way to read, so the repair is either the tiers or a scaffold escape the kernel does not yet have. workflow (workflow/manifest.json) declares no `mesh_layering` block at all. NEITHER REPAIR IS MADE HERE. This change connects the doctrine; editing a service manifest is a separate reviewable decision belonging to that manifest's owner, and doing it in the same commit would have hidden the connection behind a manifest edit.
_frozen_deferred_violations_comment: Violations covered by registry/layered-architecture-discipline/wave-3-i-deferred-manifest-violations.tsv, which defers repairs owned by manifest owners other lanes may not touch. Enumerated here rather than merely muted: an unratcheted mute is a hole, and 17 of the ledger's 24 rows currently suppress nothing, so any one of them would silently absorb a brand-new violation the day that service regresses. Frozen by the same two-sided equality as the active map — a ledger row that starts covering something new blocks, and a repaired deferral blocks until the pin here and the now-pointless ledger row come out together. The 17 rows that suppress nothing are reported in the census and deliberately NOT asserted on: striking them is the manifest owners' cleanup, and blocking on it here would make this connection hostage to a burn-down it does not own.
_frozen_manifests_without_declared_ident: Tracked manifest.json files that declare no `"microservice"`. The kernel keys every violation on a µservice name and the deferral ledger keys every row on one, so a document that names no µservice cannot be attributed and is outside the subject. The exclusion is enumerated rather than applied in silence, because deleting one key from gateway/manifest.json would otherwise be a way to walk straight out of this gate. Seven are hand-written fixtures owned by other gates' test suites; three are regulatory sovereignty/compliance pack descriptors, not workloads; observability/diagnostics/manifest.json is a real service manifest that keys itself on `"slug"` instead — declaring `"microservice"` there would bring it into the subject, which is progress and blocks here until this list is updated in the same change.
